title: A Generalization of Sárközy's theorem in function fields
summary: Sárközy's theorem says that if $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$ has positive upper asymptotic density, then there are distinct $a_1, a_2 \in A$ and $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $a_1-a_2 = n^2$. The same is true if $n^2$ is replaced by $F(n)$ for any polynomial $F \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with constant term zero. Green proved an $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$-analog of Sárközy's theorem with strong quantitative bounds, but required a technical condition on the number of roots of the polynomial $F \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$. This condition was recently removed by Li and Sauermann. In this paper, we generalize Green's argument…
